translation_en:
Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to us; Uqayl narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Malik ibn Aws al-Nasri informed me. Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mutim had mentioned some of this to me, so I went to Malik and asked him. He said: I went to Umar. His doorkeeper, Yarfa, came to him and said, “Will you admit Uthman, Abd al-Rahman, al-Zubayr, and Sad? They are asking permission.” He said, “Yes.” They entered, greeted him, and sat down. Umar then said, “Will you admit Ali and Abbas?” He gave them permission. Abbas said, “Commander of the Faithful, judge between me and this wrongdoer.” They had argued with one another. The group—Uthman and his companions—said, “Commander of the Faithful, judge between them and relieve one of them of the other.” Umar said, “Wait. I adjure you by Allah, by whose permission the heavens and earth stand: Do you know that the Messenger of Allah said, ‘We prophets are not inherited from; what we leave is charity’?” He meant that the Messenger of Allah was referring to himself. The group replied, “He did say that.” Umar turned to Ali and Abbas and said, “I adjure you both by Allah: Do you know that the Messenger of Allah said that?” They replied, “Yes.” Umar said: “I will tell you about this matter. Allah granted His Messenger a special portion of this property, which He gave to no one else. Allah says: ‘Whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from them—you did not spur horses or camels for it’ (59:6), and the rest of the verse. This was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah. By Allah, he did not keep it away from you or claim it for himself over you; he gave it to you and distributed it among you, until only this property remained. The Prophet used to provide his family’s annual maintenance from this property, then take what remained and place it in the public treasury. The Prophet continued to do this throughout his life. I adjure you by Allah: Do you know this?” They said, “Yes.” Then he said to Ali and Abbas, “I adjure you both by Allah: Do you know this?” They said, “Yes.”
“Then Allah took His Prophet. Abu Bakr said, ‘I am the successor of the Messenger of Allah,’ and took charge of it, managing it as the Messenger of Allah had managed it. At that time, you”—he turned to Ali and Abbas—“claimed that Abu Bakr had done such-and-such with it, while Allah knew that he was truthful, virtuous, rightly guided, and following the truth. Then Allah took Abu Bakr, and I said, ‘I am the successor of the Messenger of Allah and of Abu Bakr.’ I took charge of it for two years and managed it as the Messenger of Allah and Abu Bakr had managed it. Then the two of you came to me, united in your claim and in your affair: you came asking me for your share from your nephew, and this one came asking me for his wife’s share from her father. I said, ‘If you wish, I will hand it over to you, on the condition that you make a covenant and pledge to Allah that you will manage it as the Messenger of Allah managed it, as Abu Bakr managed it, and as I have managed it since I took charge of it. Otherwise, do not speak to me about it.’ You said, ‘Hand it over to us on that condition.’ So I handed it over to you on that condition. I adjure you by Allah: Did I hand it over to them on that condition?” The group said, “Yes.” He turned to Ali and Abbas and said, “I adjure you both by Allah: Did I hand it over to you on that condition?” They replied, “Yes.” Umar said, “Are you now asking me to judge otherwise? By the One by whose permission the heavens and earth stand, I will not judge this matter differently until the Hour is established. If you are unable to manage it, return it to me, and I will manage it for you.”
